## Historical audit — S0075

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/ablation_r1/ours_without_regression_guidance/C1/test/commons_155212263/trajectory.jsonl`. Only chunk 2 of 2 and the text of its observations are available; the referenced images are not visible to this audit.

| Evidence | Finding |
|---|---|
| Line 18, student model request, characters [0,277455) | **Goal:** reconstruct an indoor photograph as separate Blender/SceneAct meshes, matching camera, framing, materials and placement. The student *interpreted* the scene as a metalworking workshop with benches, wheels, an anvil, machinery and cans; that interpretation is not independently verified here. |
| Line 18, embedded student programs and step 1 feedback, [0,277455) | The first build timed out after approximately 600 seconds with no observable render: a **technical interruption**, not evidence of a visual or algorithmic failure. The student then reduced repeated geometry and hardware and used a procedural floor shader. Step 2 reported success and a saved render. |
| Line 18, embedded review and revised program, [0,277455) | After receiving the step 2 render, the student described too much room, small machinery and an exposed wall top. It hypothesized that moving the camera closer and changing its aim would improve foreground scale and parallax. The next program changed camera position/aim while retaining the 36 mm lens; it also changed floor shader coordinates and mortar size, so the revision was not exclusively a camera change. |
| Line 16, execution result step 3, [0,109918); line 17, select event; line 20, student response | Step 3 reported `ok: true`, completed 16 render samples and saved `final.png` and `scene.blend`. The recorded selection was step 3, followed by `DONE`. This establishes **formal execution/render success**, not reconstruction correctness. |
| Line 18, embedded code, [0,277455) | Multiple semantic objects are constructed, including benches, two wheel assemblies, an anvil, vice-like objects and containers. Wheel rims, hubs and spokes are grouped; support heights are manually specified, without bind dependencies. Procedural floor, roughness and emissive glass materials, camera and area lights are configured. These operations do not verify actual part contact, visibility, pose, texture fidelity, lighting quality or image match. |
| Lines 18–20; line 19 student session | The visible input includes general reconstruction instructions and a post-render review prompt, which the student followed with a camera-focused revision. No separate teacher diagnosis or teacher-proposed update is visible in this chunk, so teacher receipt or adoption cannot be asserted. The final session had no tool calls; the iterative code revision and render comparison are the visible autonomous exploration. |

**Lessons and uncertainty.** The transferable observation is that simplifying a timed-out build was followed by a successful execution; the timeout’s precise cause remains unproven. The camera and floor adjustments are task-specific hypotheses, not demonstrated improvements. Neither reference nor render pixels can be independently inspected here, so object coverage, connections, crops, pose and camera/light problems remain unresolved; no formal visual score or partial-correctness judgment is supported.
